findings.body: The canonicalization and containment check are separate from `File::open`, so an attacker who can modify the directory tree can swap a symlink or path component after validation and before the open. The final path can then resolve outside `root`, bypassing the traversal check. Use a directory-handle-relative open mechanism with appropriate no-follow or beneath-root guarantees, or otherwise make validation and opening atomic.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker replaces a validated path component with a symlink between `strip_prefix` and `File::open`; the open follows the new link and reads an arbitrary file outside `root`.
findings.title: Open through a race-resistant directory handle

findings.body: This adds two synchronous filesystem canonicalization traversals before every file open, replacing a single open operation. In a report-serving path that opens many reports, the extra metadata I/O can add measurable latency and filesystem load; consider canonicalizing and retaining the root once at a higher layer, then minimizing per-request path resolution while preserving the containment check.
findings.failure_scenario: When a caller opens many reports, each call performs root and candidate canonicalization before opening the file, multiplying filesystem metadata operations and increasing request latency.
findings.title: Avoid repeated filesystem canonicalization on every open

ground_truth.clean_trap: An untrusted name is joined to a root, but both paths are canonicalized and strip_prefix enforces containment before opening.

findings.body: This replaces a single `loadMany(ids)` operation with one sequential repository request per identifier. If `ids` can be influenced or is otherwise large, a single call now causes O(n) round trips and holds the operation open for the sum of all request latencies, increasing timeout and denial-of-service risk. Retain batching or enforce a bounded input size/concurrency strategy while applying the filters.
findings.failure_scenario: If a caller supplies a very large identifier list, the loop performs one blocking repository request for every element, causing excessive backend load and potentially timing out the request where the previous bulk call would have completed.
findings.title: Preserve batched loading to avoid per-ID resource exhaustion

findings.body: The previous implementation used `loadMany(ids)`, but this change performs one repository call per ID and awaits each call serially. The existing batch API should be retained or an equivalent batch operation should be added before applying the active-owner filter.
findings.failure_scenario: When `ids` contains many entries, each ID incurs a separate sequential database or network round trip, causing latency to grow with the input size and potentially exhausting repository or connection-pool capacity.
findings.title: Batch the repository loads

findings.body: `ResultListFactory` has a single caller and only wraps an empty list literal, adding an unnecessary abstraction with no behavior or configuration. Initialize the result list directly.
findings.title: Use a list literal instead of the one-use factory

findings.body: `ResultListFactory`, `ResultListFactory.create`, and `enrich` are publicly accessible declarations, but the change adds no Dart doc comments explaining their purpose, filtering behavior, or asynchronous loading semantics.
findings.title: Document the exported enrichment API

findings.title: Preserve the existing object return contract

findings.body: The containment check is separated from opening the file: `candidate` is canonicalized and checked, then its path is resolved again by `File::open`. An attacker who can modify the directory can replace a path component or the final file with a symlink after `strip_prefix` succeeds, causing the opened file to be outside `root`. Use a directory-relative, no-follow/atomic open mechanism appropriate for the supported platforms instead of reopening the checked canonical path.
findings.failure_scenario: After canonicalization confirms a file under `root`, an attacker swaps that file or one of its parent directories for a symlink before `File::open` runs, causing the function to read an attacker-selected file outside the permitted root.
findings.title: Use an atomic, symlink-safe open to prevent path traversal

findings.body: Replacing `repository.loadMany(ids)` with one `repository.load(id)` call per input turns a bulk operation into N individual repository operations. For large ID lists or remote repositories, this can cause latency and backend load to grow linearly and may defeat batching, connection pooling, or repository-level limits implemented by `loadMany`. Load the items in bulk and apply the predicates to the returned collection.
findings.failure_scenario: When a caller supplies a large list of IDs, enrichment performs one repository request per ID instead of one bulk request, causing request latency and repository resource consumption to increase with the list size and potentially timing out or triggering rate limits.
findings.title: Preserve bulk loading to avoid an N+1 repository call pattern

findings.body: ResultListFactory adds an abstraction with one caller and no behavior beyond constructing an ArrayList. Removing it and constructing the list directly would reduce indirection and unnecessary code.

findings.body: `ioutil.ReadFile` loads the entire fixed file into memory synchronously on every `FetchUser` call, while both the contents and any read error are discarded. If the working directory can contain a large or unexpectedly modified `defaults.json`, repeated calls can cause excessive memory use and latency; the `timeout` argument does not constrain this operation.
findings.failure_scenario: A service repeatedly invokes `FetchUser` while `defaults.json` is very large, causing each request to allocate the full file and perform a blocking read, potentially exhausting memory or making requests time out.
findings.title: Bound and handle the defaults file read

findings.body: The change introduces the deprecated `io/ioutil` package. Use the `os` package's `ReadFile` API instead, adding the corresponding import and updating the call.
findings.failure_scenario: When building with current Go tooling, deprecation checks report `io/ioutil` usage and future compatibility becomes harder as the legacy package is removed from normal guidance.
findings.title: Replace deprecated ioutil with os.ReadFile

findings.body: Removing the default changes calls that omit `timeoutMs` from receiving `30000` to receiving `undefined`. If callers pass this value into request configuration, the request layer may disable its timeout and allow connections to hang indefinitely.

findings.anchor: return [{ id, fetchedAt: new Date().toGMTString() }, timeoutMs];
findings.body: The function now returns an array containing an object and a separate timeout, and changes the timestamp from ISO 8601 to RFC 1123. Existing consumers reading result.id, result.timeoutMs, or parsing the ISO timestamp will no longer receive the same compatible result.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller reads fetchUser(id).id or fetchUser(id).timeoutMs, but the result is an array so those properties are undefined; consumers expecting an ISO 8601 fetchedAt value may also fail to parse the new GMT string.
findings.suggestion: return { id, timeoutMs, fetchedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
findings.title: Preserve the existing fetchUser result shape and timestamp format

findings.body: The containment check is separated from `File::open`, so the filesystem can change after `canonicalize` and `strip_prefix` succeed. A concurrent attacker who can modify a path component or replace the final file with a symlink can redirect this open outside `root`, bypassing the intended traversal protection. Use an OS-level directory-relative, no-symlink/ beneath check (such as `openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH` where available) rather than canonicalize-then-open.
findings.failure_scenario: After `candidate` passes the prefix check, an attacker replaces a candidate path component or file with a symlink to an external file; `File::open(candidate)` follows the changed path and opens the external file.
findings.title: Open the validated path atomically

findings.body: `candidate.canonicalize()` performs a full filesystem path resolution before `File::open(candidate)` resolves the same path again. This adds redundant metadata and symlink traversal work to every call; if `open_report` is used repeatedly, the extra filesystem I/O increases latency.
findings.failure_scenario: When many reports are opened, each call canonicalizes the candidate and then opens it by path, causing two path-resolution passes per report instead of one.
findings.title: Avoid resolving the path twice

ground_truth.clean_trap: An untrusted name is joined to a root, but both paths are canonicalized and strip_prefix enforces containment before opening.

findings.body: The prepared statement is allocated on every call but is not explicitly closed. Because this method returns the ResultSet, callers that do not close the result set promptly can leave server-side statements and client resources open until garbage collection, allowing repeated requests to exhaust database resources. Refactor the API to consume the result inside a try-with-resources block, or otherwise define and enforce statement/result-set ownership.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller repeatedly invokes find and retains or fails to close the returned ResultSet; each invocation leaves its prepared statement open, eventually exhausting the database connection's statement or resource limits and causing subsequent queries to fail.
findings.title: Close the prepared statement to prevent resource exhaustion

findings.body: `String.toLowerCase()` uses the JVM's default locale, so the same user ID can normalize to different values depending on server locale. Identity lookups should use an explicitly defined normalization policy; if lowercase matching is intended, use `Locale.ROOT` and ensure the stored IDs follow the same policy.
findings.failure_scenario: The service runs under a locale such as Turkish and receives an ID containing `I`; the lookup normalizes it differently from the value stored under the default locale, causing the wrong account lookup result or a legitimate account to become inaccessible.
